RagShortTexts: Unloading, portage and guides add time and cost.

Variants.Content: Some Dnieper rapids require sounding, lighter loads or carriage ashore. Every transfer needs guards and labor. A lightly loaded boat passing does not establish a route for the whole shipment; current water conditions decide.
Rapids split guards between boats, cargo and carriers. A defined reunion point prevents the advance from moving on while food remains behind.
River freight includes guides and transfer labor. Pricing by water distance alone leaves shipments without willing workers at difficult reaches.
Shore carriers face injury and loss claims. Counting parcels and assigning watchers takes time but clarifies responsibility when goods go missing.
